messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: compiling error for vector(M)
parts:
In example vol2/jaws, I have

transformed parameters {
vector(M) mu;
for (m in 1:M) mu[m] <- beta0 + beta1 * age[m];
}

where M is defined in the Data block.

The cpp code could not be compiled here though it works if it is
`vector(4) mu.'

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] compiling error for vector(M) [due to "most vexing parse"]
parts:
Believe it or not, there's an entire Wikipedia
page devoted to this "feature" of the C++ parser
and its unexpected consequences:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_vexing_parse

As the Wikipedia says, Clang gives a good error
message, which is how I found the Wikipedia entry:

src/demo/jaws.cpp:183:20: warning: parentheses were disambiguated as a
function declarator
vector_v mu(vector_v(M));

Eh?

Lucky for us, the Wikpedia describes the magic
pixie dust required to get a more reasonable
behavior out of the constructor. A magic layer of
parens:

vector_v mu((vector_v(M)));

I'll commit a fix to the code generator ASAP.

The web is so awesome.

- Bob

P.S. reminds me of Boost's recommended disambiguation
of isnan as (boost::math::isnan)(x) so that "isnan"
isn't expanded as a macro.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] variable declarations patched
parts:
Variable declarations were trickier than I thought, but the bugs
in variable declaration generation that Jiqiang
found (see mail chain below) are now patched and the compiled
models are now parsing for:

src/models/bugs_examples/vol2/jaws/jaws.stan
src/models/bugs_examples/vol2/mvn_orange/mvn_orange.stan

----------------

The following details are probably only interesting if
you spent the last few hours with pencil and paper and
C++ compiler.

After fixing the "most vexing parse", the problem with
which is that

var a(var());

isn't taken as an initialization of a to var(), I
introduced a simpler, but related parsing ambiguity,
which Jiqiang also found:

var a(); // variable a of type var
// initialized with nullary constructor var()
var b = a; // OK

double a(); // a declared as nullary function returning double
double b = a; // DOH!

What I needed was a slightly more nuanced base case
for the recursive generation of types:

var a(var()); // copy constructor
var b = a; // OK

double a(double()); // init to default 0
double b = a; // OK

but that was too ugly to bear, so I cleaned up the
base case so the declarations are the way I'd write
them by hand (now that I understand the ambiguities
mentioned above):

var a; // variable a of type var init with nullary ctor var()
var b = a; // OK

double a; // declaration of variable a
double b = a; // OK

- Bob
